_comment: EC2 Security Group export (task 8.1). Original home: the EC2 instance's Security Group, not a file on the host. Rendered from the AWS console rules; placeholders must never be replaced with real account IDs before committing.
description: Mini SOC single-instance lab: 22/80 open to the internet for the attack target demo, 22/80/443 also used for analysis access.

inbound_rules.purpose: SSH attack target for ssh-brute-force.sh / live IDS SSH-brute-force detection
DVWA target for the web-attack scripts (sqli/xss/cmdi/traversal/bruteforce), default_server on port 80
SOC dashboard + /api proxy; analyst-only, not the attack surface

outbound_rules.purpose: apt/package installs; logs SOC_OUT: on the host so unusual_outbound can fire

notes: Port 80 is required for web-attack-sim tests; it must stay reachable.
Port 443 is restricted to the analyst's /32 because it is not part of the attack demo; use the host firewall to log accepted traffic.
The nftables rules in nftables.conf are the second layer; the Security Group is the perimeter. Both must be kept in sync.
